title: Building a library of models with liblex
text: Traditional memory-based learning (MBL) methods fit new local model query observation. effective, per-query refitting can computationally expensive requires access full reference library prediction time. liblex() function (library localised experts) takes different approach: pre-computes library local models build phase, retrieves combines relevant experts prediction time without refitting. design offers several advantages: Computational efficiency: Models fitted ; prediction requires retrieval weighted averaging. Privacy preservation: model coefficients centroids need stored (original training spectra). Intrinsic uncertainty: Disagreement among retrieved experts provides natural measure prediction uncertainty. Interpretability: expert retains regression coefficients variable importance, enabling inspection local relationships. method introduced described detail Ramirez-Lopez et al. (2026).

title: Building a library of models with liblex
text: liblex algorithm operates two phases: Anchor selection: subset reference observations (anchors) selected. anchor generate one local expert model. default, observations serve anchors; large datasets, representative subset can specified via anchor_indices. Neighborhood construction: anchor, kk nearest neighbors identified full reference set using dissimilarity measure. Note neighbors drawn reference observations, just anchors. Local model fitting: partial least squares (PLS) regression model (variant weigthed average PLS modified PLS) fitted within neighborhood, producing regression coefficients. neighborhood centroid stored use prediction. Validation (optional): Nearest-neighbor cross-validation assesses performance optimizes hyperparameters (kk PLS component range). Expert retrieval: new observation, dissimilarities stored centroids computed, kk nearest experts retrieved. optimal kk determined fitting used , number anchors least large maximum kk evaluated. Weighted combination: retrieved expert generates prediction. predictions combined via distance-based kernel weighting, closer experts receiving higher weights. Uncertainty estimation: weighted variance across expert predictions provides per-sample uncertainty estimate, reflecting disagreement among retrieved experts.

text: function assesses whether dissimilarity matrix captures meaningful structure examining side information nearest neighbor pairs (Ramirez-Lopez et al., 2013). observations similar dissimilarity space also similar side information values, dissimilarity considered effective. numeric side_info, root mean square differences (RMSD) observation nearest neighbor computed: \[j() = NN(x_i, X^{{-}})\] \[RMSD = \sqrt{\frac{1}{m} \sum_{=1}^{m} (y_i - y_{j()})^2}\] \(NN(x_i, X^{-})\) returns index nearest neighbor observation \(\) (excluding ), \(y_i\) side information value observation \(\), \(m\) number observations. categorical side_info, kappa index computed: \[\kappa = \frac{p_o - p_e}{1 - p_e}\] \(p_o\) observed agreement \(p_e\) agreement expected chance.
